questionText: How many moles of electrons are required to deposit $27\text{ g}$ of aluminium metal from molten alumina ($Al_2O_3$)? (Atomic mass of $Al = 27\text{ u}$)

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Molar Charge for Deposition of Polyvalent Ions (Electrochemistry):
Molar mass of $Al = 27\text{ g/mol}$, so $27\text{ g} = 1.0\text{ mol}$ of $Al$.
The half-cell reaction is $Al^{3+} + 3e^- \to Al(s)$.
Therefore, 1 mole of $Al$ requires 3 moles of electrons ($3\text{ F} = 3 \times 96500\text{ C}$).

Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.
